# Mobile, but faster

**Product Update — [Date]**

We've spent the last two release cycles focused on a single question: why does the app feel slower on a phone than it does on a laptop? Today's release is the answer to that question — and the fix.

## What changed

**Faster cold starts.** We rebuilt how the app loads on launch, deferring non-essential work until after the first screen is interactive. Cold start time is down from 4.1s to 1.6s on mid-tier Android devices.

**Smaller download, smaller footprint.** We removed unused dependencies, switched to modern image formats, and split our JavaScript bundle so you only download the code for the screen you're actually looking at. The app is now 38% smaller on disk.

**Smoother scrolling.** Long lists — your inbox, search results, activity feed — now recycle views instead of rendering everything at once. Scrolling holds a steady 60fps on devices where it previously dropped into the 30s.

**Better offline and low-signal behavior.** We cache more aggressively and retry failed requests intelligently instead of leaving you staring at a spinner. Actions taken offline now queue and sync when you reconnect.

**Less battery drain.** Background sync now batches network calls and respects system power-saving modes. Early telemetry shows a 22% reduction in energy use during typical sessions.

## Why it matters

More than half of our sessions happen on mobile, and a growing share of those are on older devices and slower networks. Performance isn't a nice-to-have there — it's the difference between finishing a task and abandoning it. We've moved our internal targets to reflect that: every release is now benchmarked against a mid-tier Android device on a simulated 3G connection, not a flagship phone on office Wi-Fi.

## What's next

We're not done. Next up:

- Predictive prefetching so common navigation paths feel instant
- Faster image loading with progressive placeholders
- Reducing time-to-interactive on the three heaviest screens in the app

## Get the update

Update from the App Store or Google Play, or wait for auto-update to roll out over the next few days. No action needed on your end — the improvements apply automatically.

As always, if something feels slow, tell us. Performance reports from real users on real devices have driven most of what's in this release. Reach us at [support link] or tap **Help → Report an issue** in the app.

# Mobile Performance: The Fixes Are Live

**Release [X.Y] — [Date]**

The mobile slowdown is fixed. Details below.

## Cold start: 4.1s → 1.6s

We deferred non-essential initialization until after first interactive paint. Analytics, feature-flag hydration, and prefetch warming now run post-render instead of blocking it. Measured on the mid-tier Android reference device, not a flagship.

## Bundle: 38% smaller

Dropped four unused dependencies, moved to AVIF/WebP across the board, and code-split by route. You now pull down the screen you asked for, not the whole app.

## Scroll: locked at 60fps

List virtualization is in. Inbox, search results, and the activity feed recycle views rather than rendering the full set. The frame drops into the 30s on long lists are gone.

## Offline behavior

Broader cache coverage, exponential backoff on retries, and an action queue that flushes on reconnect. The indefinite spinner on flaky connections should no longer be reproducible — if you hit it, file it.

## Battery: −22%

Background sync batches network calls and honors Doze / Low Power Mode. Telemetry is from the beta cohort over two weeks, so treat it as directional until we have broader data.

## Benchmark target has moved

We now gate releases against the mid-tier Android device on simulated 3G. Flagship-on-Wi-Fi numbers are no longer sufficient to ship. This is the change most likely to affect your work — budget accordingly.

## Next

- Predictive prefetch on common navigation paths
- Progressive image placeholders
- TTI work on the three heaviest screens

Rolling out over the next few days via standard auto-update.
